subject: TruNorth audit: request for extended log retention evidence and variance
messages:
From: Carla Mendes <carla.mendes@trunorth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: 12-month tenant log retention evidence and variance

Hi Jonas,

We're starting our annual IT audit and TruNorth's auditors have asked us to confirm that vendor tenant-scoped operational logs can be retained for 12 months in order to meet regulatory sampling requirements. Our default expectation is 90 days, but we need a formal variance / exception and supporting evidence (SIG/CAIQ answers, SOC 2 artifact references, and a sample export or attestation).

Attached is a short requirements packet from our auditor that lists the exact items (trunorth_audit_requirements.pdf). Key asks:
- Confirmation whether Redwood can retain per-tenant request & audit logs for 12 months (and whether this applies to Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments).
- A matrix of which log types are affected (request, access, debug, KV-cache traces, etc.) and how they will be exported or preserved.
- A redacted sample export or a deletion attestation workflow showing proof-of-delete when the variance is rescinded.
- Any SOC 2 scope or auditor contact we can provide to our team.

Can you loop in the security/controls folks and let us know what evidence you can provide and a realistic timeline — our audit kickoff is Nov 16.

Thanks,
Carla Mendes
Compliance Manager
TruNorth Financial

Attachments: trunorth_audit_requirements.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Irene, Marissa — forwarding TruNorth's ask. Brief summary / asks from Carla: can we support a 12-month tenant-scoped retention for their logs (they're a financial customer and need it for audit sampling), and what evidence can we deliver by Nov 16.

Specifics they want: (1) confirmation for Hosted/Dedicated/Private, (2) a mapping of log types and preservation/export plan, (3) sample export or attestation, (4) SOC 2/auditor contact.

My initial notes:
- Hosted (our standard multi-tenant) currently enforces 90d rolling logs for most runtime traces; we have technical prefixes and KV cache material that we consider ephemeral.
- Dedicated/Private customers can retain longer with config changes or by enabling tenant-level archival to customer-controlled buckets.
- We may be able to provide a temporary variance (retention carveout) for Hosted via a saved snapshot export service for specific tenant IDs, but this will require product/security sign-off (and possibly a short-term cost add-on).

Can you:
1) Confirm technical feasibility and recommended approach (hosted path vs dedicated/private).
2) Support generation of a mapping spreadsheet for Carla: which logs we can preserve, where we store them, retention controls, encryption/KMS notes.
3) Provide a short attestation template or a redacted sample export we can deliver by Nov 16 (or an alternative timeline).

Marissa — can you own the customer communication once we have an answer and be ready to discuss PO/timing/costs?

Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the ping — quick technical/controls summary below. I've attached a proposed mapping workbook (redwood_log-retention-mapping.xlsx) that aligns with TruNorth's asks.

Short answer: Yes, we can support a 12-month tenant-scoped retention for the specific request/audit logs they listed, but the approach differs by deployment mode and has operational tradeoffs.

Proposed options (high level):
1) Dedicated / Private: simplest. Enable tenant-level archival to a customer-managed object store or allocate dedicated archival buckets in our infra with 12mo TTL. We can provide signed export manifests and an auditable retention policy.

2) Hosted (multi-tenant): not enabled by default. Two workable paths:
   a) Temporary snapshot export: we can run a controlled export of the requested log types for the tenant into an encrypted object store (S3) for 12 months. The export will be namespaced and access-restricted; we provide MD5 manifests and a deletion attestation when retention ends. This is the least intrusive and preserves our multi-tenant isolation.
   b) Tenant-retention flag: we could enable a per-tenant retention flag (engineering effort + cost delta) to keep full request/audit logs for 12 months in our standard pipeline. This is heavier operationally and requires a written variance and security sign-off.

Controls/evidence we can produce:
- Completed SIG rows that map to log retention controls (we can mark which controls are in-scope for the variance).
- CAIQ references for logging and retention fields.
- SOC 2: we can provide a SOC 2 Type II report excerpt (log retention control statement) and a contact for our auditor for attestation requests.
- Redacted sample export: we can produce a redacted export (PII removed) and a proof-of-export manifest.
- Proof-of-delete/attestation template for when variance expires.

Operational notes / timeline:
- If TruNorth accepts a snapshot-export approach, we can deliver the mapping + sample export and auditor contact within 10 business days (target Nov 13).
- Enabling a tenant-retention flag (persisting logs in-platform for 12 months) will take longer (engineering + security sign-off) — estimate 4–6 weeks and likely a formal variance/MOU.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm with Carla whether a snapshot-export to be held by Redwood is acceptable or if they require logs to remain in-platform.
2) If snapshot is OK, we deliver the mapping workbook, redacted sample export, manifest, and SOC 2 excerpt by Nov 13.
3) Marissa: I'll need the customer PO / approval to create the snapshot export job (covers storage and operational effort).

Attaching: redwood_log-retention-mapping.xlsx

Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
